mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 2% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a financial crisis.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in Real Personal Consumption Expenditures (GDPC1) exceeding 3% indicates weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during a supply shock.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 8% for three consecutive months signals labor market distress, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect fails during a period of aggressive monetary easing.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not observed during a global supply chain shock.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both Real Personal Consumption Expenditures (GDPC1) and Housing Starts (HOUST) signals broad-based demand weakness, which amplifies recession risk and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during a monetary policy shock.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1% combined with a concurrent decline in Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below 1% signals a deflationary easing cycle, which increases risk appetite and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% AND CPIAUCSL < 101 (i.e., CPI < 1% YoY) in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a banking crisis.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) above 100,000 for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during a wage-price spiral.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase in Real Personal Consumption Expenditures (GDPC1) and Industrial Production (INDPRO) above 0.5% signals synchronized demand and supply expansion, which raises earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, except during periods of extreme inflation.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect fails when CPIAUCSL YoY > 10%.
